purpose: Continuously raise player-perceived quality instead of treating feature presence or source binding as completion.

MOTION.description: Locomotion, idle, turn, attack, hit, death and weight transfer feel visibly authored rather than root-only or micro-bob.

COMBAT_FEEL.description: Anticipation, impact, recoil, hit readability and action feedback are immediately perceptible without changing combat authority.

UI_HUD.description: Hierarchy, readability, touch targets, safe areas, overlap, state feedback and screen density remain commercial-quality.

INVENTORY_EQUIPMENT.description: Acquisition, inventory, equip/unequip and equipped-state feedback are discoverable and visibly confirm state changes.

AUDIO_MUSIC.description: At least one active runtime audio layer exists and music/SFX state supports gameplay context without masking important cues.

VFX.description: Telegraphs, impacts and signature events use readable intensity hierarchy and never obscure required play information.

CAMERA.description: Follow, framing, impact response and focus hierarchy feel responsive while preserving mobile readability and telegraphs.

WORLD_ART_LIGHTING.description: World materials, lighting, landmarks, atmosphere and environment dressing communicate region identity and gameplay risk.

ONBOARDING_READABILITY.description: The first playable state communicates objective and next action without a blocking tutorial wall.

MOBILE_INPUT.description: Primary actions remain touchable, responsive and safe-area aware with no hidden or undersized essential control.

PERFORMANCE_STABILITY.description: Presentation buildup stays within runtime memory/scene complexity budgets and does not regress stability.

notes: Animator/Motor6D presence alone is insufficient; actual movement/action or active AnimationTrack evidence is required.
Sound instances alone are insufficient; at least one runtime-playing sound is required for commercial audio acceptance.
Inventory/equipment games must show a discoverable surface and an observed state-changing action when such an action is exercised.
Canvas/CSS source markers cannot replace real browser-visible change.
Unity Web development-floor evidence is compatibility/runtime evidence; native promotion still requires native runtime proof.
